r: Made Peshwa by **Shahu (1713)**; **streamlined administration after Sambhaji**; **1719 grant** (swarajya, chauth, sardeshmukhi of the Deccan) via the Sayyids; assigned collection areas to sardars
Most charismatic after Shivaji; **Hindu Pad Padshahi**; "**strike the trunk, the branches will fall**"; **Palkhed 1728**; Malwa, Bundelkhand; **raided Delhi 1737**; Bhopal / Doraha Sarai 1738 (Malwa)
Revived power after Panipat – beat the Nizam, Haidar Ali, Rohillas, Rajputs, Jats; died 1772

1.x: Order: **Balaji Vishwanath → Baji Rao I → Balaji Baji Rao → Madhav Rao I**.

**Peshwa as virtual ruler:** the office was hereditary from 1720; after **Shahu's death (1749)** the **Sangola agreement (1750)** made the Chhatrapati nominal – the king became a non-entity from **Balaji Baji Rao's** time, and by 1750 the state was a **confederacy presided over by the Peshwa**. Seat: **Poona** (Chhatrapati at Satara).

**Confederacy:** areas were divided among military chiefs **in Shahu's reign** (Balaji Vishwanath's assignments; organised by **Baji Rao I** to satisfy the old chiefs under **Senapati Dabhade**). Main weakness: rivalries of semi-independent chiefs.

r: "**Maratha Machiavelli / Chanakya of Maratha politics**"; led the **Barabhai**; died **1800**
Shivaji's grandson; first Maratha chief to offer **nazr at the Ajmer dargah** of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti
Irregular plundering horsemen with the **Maratha armies**; leaders **Chitu**, Karim Khan, Wasil Muhammad; crushed by **Lord Hastings (1817-18)**
Land assigned to chiefs for military service
Marathas seized **Malwa and Gujarat** from the Mughals
Baji Rao I beat **Nizam-ul-Mulk**; chauth and sardeshmukhi of the Deccan conceded
Nizam defeated; blamed **Sir John Shore's neutrality** → Subsidiary Alliance (1798)

After **Narayan Rao's murder**; **Treaty of Surat (1775)** – Bombay to back **Raghunath Rao** with 2,500 troops; **Treaty of Purandar (1776)** – **Marathas and the English** (Calcutta council) annulled Surat; **Convention of Wadgaon (1779)** rejected by **Warren Hastings**; **Treaty of Salbai (1782)** with **Mahadji Scindia** – status quo

**Treaty of Bassein (1802)** – Baji Rao II accepted Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance; **Assaye** (Arthur Wellesley vs Scindia-Bhonsle), **Laswari** (Lord Lake vs Scindia); **Deogaon** (Bhonsle: Cuttack, Balasore), **Surji-Anjangaon** (Scindia)
Governor-General **Lord Hastings**; Khadki, Koregaon, Sitabuldi, Mahidpur; **Peshwaship abolished in 1818** under **Baji Rao II**, pensioned to **Bithur near Kanpur**; small Satara state kept
Uncle of Madhav Rao I and Narayan Rao; father of Baji Rao II

2.x: **Road to the second war:** **Nana Phadnavis died (1800)** → **Holkar and Scindia fought over the weak Peshwa** (Holkar won at Poona, 1802) → Baji Rao II fled to the British.
**Chronology:** Nana Phadnavis's death (**1800**) → recall of Wellesley (**1805**) → **Vellore Mutiny (10 July 1806)** → Anglo-Nepalese war (**1814-16**).

r: **Sadashiv Rao Bhau** (overall); **Vishwas Rao** (Peshwa's son, nominal) – both killed
**Ibrahim Khan Gardi** – the Muslim commander who **died fighting for the Marathas** (loyal)

0.x: **Immediate cause:** the Marathas (Raghunath Rao, 1758) **expelled Abdali's son and viceroy Timur Shah from Lahore**.
**Causes of defeat:** **Bhau's tactical errors**, **Abdali's superior generalship**, **large numbers of non-combatants** and baggage; no northern allies (Jats, Rajputs alienated); supply collapse.
**Coded message to the Peshwa:** "**Two pearls have been dissolved, 27 gold coins lost …**" – the pearls were Vishwas Rao and Bhau.
**Result:** Maratha northern ambition halted; the vacuum helped the Company; "it decided not who was to rule India, but who was not"; recovery under **Madhav Rao I** within a decade.
